**Finding: missing — insurance clause absent (severity low).**

The agreement has no insurance obligation anywhere. The single "insurance" hit (p0051) is a Licensee-side cost allocation for taxes, duties, shipping and similar charges — not a coverage covenant. The General Provisions (p0144–p0159) go from governing law through representation by counsel with no insurance sub-section, and no other article supplies one.

Direction check: Licensor operates the hosted trading platform through which we receive consolidated market data and transmit orders and trading tickets (p0007, p0021, p0031, p0033), so it is exactly the kind of hosting vendor touching our transaction data for which the playbook treats "no insurance" as walk-away territory. The obligation therefore properly runs against Licensor, not us.

Redline (validated, ok:true): new General Provision (l) inserted after p0159 at the **preferred** limits — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, running through the term plus one year. The comment flags the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in case Licensor pushes back on the cyber limit.
